article.headline: A Designer Builds the Directory He Kept Wishing Existed
article.lede: Michał Greń, a designer, noticed himself scattering links to AI tools across ten different places — bookmarks, notes, Slack threads — and solved the problem the only way a builder can: he made a single page instead. The result is a curated index of AI agents and skills aimed specifically at designers, organized by category and updated as the ecosystem grows.
article.body:
The underlying itch is familiar to anyone watching the AI-tooling space. **Claude Code skills** — small, installable instruction packages that extend Anthropic's Claude with specialist knowledge — have proliferated quickly enough that discovery has become its own problem. There is no canonical registry, so useful tools circulate through social threads and disappear into link graveyards. Greń's directory is an attempt at curation: one page, organized by design discipline.

The screenshot shows categories spanning Accessibility, Design, Dev, and Motion, with a Hot Picks section and a Latest feed. Two featured entries illustrate the range. *Figma Designer*, attributed to Anthropic, aims to give Claude the mental model of a senior interface designer — instructing it to reason through components, *auto-layout* (Figma's responsive spacing system), and *design tokens* (named variables that store a product's visual decisions, like color and type scales) before generating anything. *Theme Factory*, also from Anthropic, offers ten ready-made visual themes — matched palettes and font pairings — that can be applied to any artifact Claude produces.

Both install the same way: `npx claude skills add <skill-name>`, a one-line command that pulls the skill into a local Claude Code environment. The simplicity of that interface is what makes the directory concept viable — skills are lightweight enough that a curated list functions like a recipe book rather than a software catalog.

The broader pattern here is worth noting. As AI capabilities expand into professional workflows, the bottleneck shifts from capability to legibility: which tools exist, what they actually do, and whether they fit a specific job. Greń's project is a small bet that a human editor, solving their own organizational frustration, can do something that algorithmic feeds cannot — build a list someone actually trusts.

concepts.definition: Installable extension packages for Anthropic's Claude Code CLI that add specialist knowledge or behaviors to Claude. A skill is essentially a curated prompt or instruction set bundled for easy distribution. Users install them with a single `npx claude skills add <name>` command, and the skill shapes how Claude approaches a specific domain — like design, accessibility, or code review.

Named variables that encode a product's visual decisions — a color called `brand-primary`, a spacing unit called `space-4`, a typeface called `heading-font`. Storing these as tokens rather than hardcoded values means a design system can change consistently across every screen and component by updating a single source. They are the connective tissue between a designer's intent and a developer's implementation.

A feature in Figma that makes frames behave like CSS flexbox containers — elements inside them reflow, resize, and maintain consistent spacing rules automatically as content changes. Understanding auto-layout is considered a marker of design-systems fluency; it is the mechanism that makes components truly responsive rather than statically sized.

repos.summary: A community hub for discovering and managing AI skills across coding tools including Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. It describes itself as indexing over 110,000 community skills, installable and trackable declaratively. Whether or not Greń's directory is built on this project, skillfile represents the infrastructure layer solving the same discovery problem from a more developer-facing angle.
